faqs.a: Sales tax is set by state, county, and city, so the combined rate depends on exactly where you buy. The US average is roughly 7 to 8% when everything is combined, but some places charge 0% and others top 10%. Check your local rate for the exact number.
faqs.q: What is the sales tax rate where I live?

faqs.a: In the US, advertised prices usually exclude sales tax, which is added at checkout. In most of Europe and many other countries, the displayed price already includes VAT. If you are traveling, do not assume the rules match home.
faqs.q: Is sales tax included in the price?

faqs.a: Sales tax applies to most physical goods and, in many places, some services and digital products. Groceries, medicine, and clothing are exempt in some states. Rules vary wildly, so this calculator just does the math - it does not decide what is taxable.

Online sellers generally must collect tax for the state where the item is delivered (destination-based sourcing), though small sellers may be exempt below certain thresholds. The total on your order confirmation is the legal amount.
faqs.q: Do I pay sales tax on online purchases?

faqs.a: Divide the tax-inclusive total by (1 + rate). A $108 total at 8% tax means the pre-tax price was 108 / 1.08 = $100. The tax was $8.
faqs.q: How do I work backwards from a total?

faqs.a: Rounding usually happens per line item or on the total, to the nearest cent. Half-cent amounts are the classic edge case: most systems round half up. The differences are pennies, but they explain why receipts sometimes differ from your mental math by a cent.
faqs.q: Why is my receipt a cent off?

sales-tax-calculator.formula:
Tax = price x (rate / 100).
Total = price + tax = price x (1 + rate / 100).
Reverse: pre-tax price = total / (1 + rate / 100).
